text:
Olivia Chen: heads up — noticed weirdly attributed quota spikes in the console after yesterday's rollout to canary. dashboard: https://console.redwood-inference/internal/dashboards/tenant-quota?snapshot=latest
James R: ugh, I saw that too in telemetry — tenant A showing requests that trace to tenant B's canary traffic
Kai M: can you paste the raw request log for one example? wondering if it's a header/tagging problem at the routing layer
Olivia Chen: paste of log snippet:
```
INFO 2026-03-20T18:13:22Z request_id=abc123 routed_to=node-7 tenant_id=tenant-a X-Forwarded-Tenant=tenant-b handler=proxy-prefetch
```
James R: that's the smoking gun — internal proxy is routing with X-Forwarded-Tenant set incorrectly during prefetch fallback
Maria S: timeline? which PR/rollout touched the prefetch routing code? I think the canary had the new affinity heuristic
Kai M: PR #4923 updated routing policy to prefer last-active region and added a prefetch path. It changed how we synthesize tenant headers when we short-circuit to cache
Olivia Chen: repro steps I used: 1) enable canary for 5% 2) run parallel quick-switches between orgs 3) hit insights panel -> saw cross-tenant rows in ~12s
James R: likely race between quota-scrubber job and prefetch proxy creating synthetic requests without proper tenant scoping. scrubber attributes metrics by request header, but prefetch sometimes reuses upstream context
Maria S: short-term: can we revert the prefetch header synth in the canary? or add defensive check in quota-scrubber to ignore requests from internal-prefetch agents
Kai M: quick patch idea: if header X-Prefetch-Agent present then require X-Origin-Tenant and X-Auth-Token match. I'll sketch it now
Olivia Chen: we should also add a telemetry flag to mark suspected cross-tenant attributions so we can filter historical data for billing impact
James R: agree. also need a postmortem entry for rollout UX — the canary binary didn't opt into the ``tenant-assertion`` middleware so it silently bypassed checks
Maria S: ops plan: 1) disable canary toggle (rollback) 2) block prefetch path in gateway config 3) deploy Kai's patch to canary staging 4) run audit to enumerate affected customers
deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback canary toggle triggered by Maria S at 2026-03-20T18:25:10Z :white_check_mark:
Olivia Chen: after rollback spikes stopped in ~30s. I'll start the audit and produce a minimal list for billing and CS handoff
Kai M: pushed PR draft with assertion check, unit test, and a simple `prefetch_agent` gate. cc @James R for scrubber changes
James R: I'll add defensive logic in quota-scrubber to ignore metrics where tenant header is mismatched with auth token. low risk change, but will add feature flag
Maria S: good. once the patch lands, let's run canary with tight observability (tenant-tagged traces + metric-breakdown) before re-enabling
Olivia Chen: thanks team. please drop short notes in the postmortem doc when you have time. tagging CS to prepare email templates if audit shows customer impact :cc: @CS-team
